# update — OpenAI Codex CLI

<!-- GENERATED by bin/docs_build.py from codex/skills/update/SKILL.md — do not edit; edit the source and run: python3 bin/docs_build.py build -->

> Check and refresh Polytropos harness installs and generated mirrors with the repository's updater. Use for install freshness, bundle drift, or an explicitly requested refresh; checking is read-only and always comes first.

- **Source:** [codex/skills/update/SKILL.md](https://github.com/agentmc15/polytropos/blob/main/codex/skills/update/SKILL.md)
- **Also available on:** [Claude Code](../claude/update.md)

## In practice

### What it does

After a pull or a merge, tells you whether what is installed still matches the repository:
harness installs, bundle files, and generated mirrors, on one card. Checking only reads.
Refreshing is a separate step that runs only when you ask for it in the current
conversation.

### When to reach for it

- Use it after pulling or merging changes into a Polytropos checkout.
- Use it when a skill or prompt behaves like an older version of itself.
- **Not** as permission to write: a freshness question is not authorization, and when the
  intent is unclear the skill shows the dry run instead.

### Worked example

```bash
python3 "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/harness_update.py" check --repo-root "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT"
python3 "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/harness_update.py" apply --repo-root "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT" --dry-run
```

The first line always runs first. Exit 3 means drift was found, not that the checker
crashed. Read the card's vocabulary literally:

| On the card | Read it as |
|---|---|
| “not installed” | absence, not a failure |
| `unmanaged` | a warning |
| `conflict`, `managed-update` | actionable Codex drift |
| `not applicable here (install source)` | not drift: project agents belong in the checkout where Codex works |

### Failure modes & fallbacks

- **`apply` reports `error`.** Stop and report it; a writer is never retried blindly.
- **A differing `AGENTS.md` or skill directory.** Those destinations are no-clobber: the
  copy is reported as `skip-differs` and preserved, and it needs your own decision.
- **Project agents or the modern plugin look stale.** They are outside this updater's
  apply scope; use the repository's Codex installer workflow when you want those surfaces
  refreshed.
- **A stale Claude plugin cache.** The updater never writes `~/.claude`. It may print a
  remedy, which runs only after separate explicit approval.

### Cost & safety

`check` and `--dry-run` write nothing and dispatch no model. A real `apply` may overwrite
Copilot bundle-owned files and Codex generated compatibility prompts, listing the ones that
differed; unknown files stay untouched. Pricing values and documentation snapshot tables are
never refreshed by this engine. The JSON modes and the human apply card can contain absolute
home paths, so scrub local paths before sharing output.

## The skill card — what the model reads

This is the SKILL.md body the model reads, transformed for this page: the source's own leading title, if it had one, is removed; every remaining heading is demoted one level to nest under this section; and relative links are rewritten to site or GitHub URLs. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `{{POLYTROPOS_ROOT}}` are install-time path variables, left intact exactly as the model sees them. The unmodified original is [codex/skills/update/SKILL.md](https://github.com/agentmc15/polytropos/blob/main/codex/skills/update/SKILL.md).

Resolve `POLYTROPOS_ROOT` from this skill's location. In a managed copy use `POLYTROPOS_ROOT="{{POLYTROPOS_ROOT}}"`; reject the literal placeholder. Confirm `$POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/harness_update.py` exists before running it.

Always begin with the read-only check and report its card:

```bash
python3 "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/harness_update.py" check --repo-root "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT"
```

Exit 3 means drift was found, not that the checker crashed. “not installed” is absence, `unmanaged` is a warning, and Codex `conflict` or `managed-update` entries are actionable drift.

Project agents reported `not applicable here (install source)` are not drift: the root is the checkout the Claude marketplace installs from, which never carries `.codex/agents/`. They belong in the checkout where Codex works; never install them into the install source.

### Write boundary

Run `apply` only when the user explicitly requested a refresh in the current conversation. A freshness question is not authorization to write. If intent is unclear, show the dry-run instead:

```bash
python3 "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/harness_update.py" apply --repo-root "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT" --dry-run
```

After explicit authorization, run:

```bash
python3 "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/harness_update.py" apply --repo-root "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT"
```

Stop and report an `error` result; do not retry a writer blindly.

### Interpret apply accurately

- Copilot bundle-owned files may be overwritten; unknown files remain untouched. A `preserved` entry is intentional and needs a separate user decision.
- Codex generated compatibility prompts may be overwritten and are listed when they differ. User-editable `AGENTS.md` and skill destinations are no-clobber: differing copies are reported as `skip-differs` and preserved.
- Project `.codex/agents/*.toml` files and the modern Codex plugin are outside this updater's apply scope. Use the repository's Codex installer workflow separately when the user requests those surfaces.
- Generated repository mirrors are refreshed by their existing sync tools. Pricing values and documentation snapshot tables still require the repository's documented human refresh procedure.
- The updater never writes `~/.claude`. It may print a conditional stale-cache remedy; run that remedy only after separate explicit approval.

The check and apply JSON modes have different shapes, and JSON plus the human apply card can contain absolute home paths. Scrub local paths before sharing output outside the machine.

Finish with what was observed, what changed, any preserved/conflicting paths described without leaking the home directory, and remaining limitations.
